Release Highlights
October 14, 2026

A fix release. Long meetings that failed to summarize with Built-in AI now work, a failed save no longer puts your recording at risk, summary templates are one click away, and your AI assistant sees the speaker names you saved.
Long meetings now summarize with Built-in AI instead of failing with "Failed to add token to batch"
A failed save of one piece of your recording no longer puts the rest of it at risk
Summary templates are one click away from the meeting page and from Settings > Summary
Speaker names you saved now show in your AI assistant, the command-line tool and exports
Recording keeps going when some audio can't be transcribed, and meetilypro:// links work on Mac when Meetily is closed
Table of Contents
What's New in Pro 1.11.1

Meetily Pro 1.11.1, released on October 14, 2026, is a fix release for Built-in AI summaries and recording. Long meetings that used to fail now summarize with Built-in AI, and a failed save no longer puts your recording at risk. Summary templates are now one click away, and your AI assistant sees the speaker names you saved. There are no breaking changes and nothing to migrate. Meetily still records and transcribes on your own Windows or Mac computer, with no bot joining the call.
If you are on Pro 1.11.0, this is a normal in-place update.
Long Meetings Now Summarize With Built-in AI
With Built-in AI, a long meeting could fail to summarize with the error "Failed to add token to batch". The transcript was too long for the model to read in one go.

Meetily now splits a long transcript into parts sooner, before it gets too long for the model, then summarizes each part and combines them into one summary. Short meetings still summarize in a single pass, the same as before.
A long meeting now takes several steps, so it takes longer to summarize. On a laptop, a very long meeting can take half an hour or more. Let it run.
This release also includes summary fixes for the Qwen 3.5 2B model, so its summaries repeat themselves less.
Safer Recordings

While you record, Meetily saves your audio in small pieces and joins them when you stop. Before, if saving one piece failed, the pieces after it could fail too, and the recording could be lost. Now Meetily recovers from a failed save and keeps saving the rest of your recording.

Recording also keeps going when some audio can't be transcribed. Before, a transcription problem could stop your recording. Now the recording continues, and after you stop, Meetily tells you the transcript may have gaps. You can then transcribe the meeting again.
Summary Templates, One Click Away
Summary templates help you get the right kind of summary for each meeting, such as a daily standup, a sales call or a retrospective. They are now easier to reach:
The new Summary Template button, next to Model Settings on the meeting page.
Settings > Summary.

children.alt: Meetily Pro meeting page: the new Summary Template button, highlighted, between Model Settings and Generate Summary in the action bar

children.text: Speaker Names in Your AI Assistant, CLI and Exports
When you name the speakers in a meeting, those names now show everywhere you read the transcript:
Your AI assistant, when it is connected to Meetily (for example Claude, Cursor or Windsurf). See the Meetily MCP server.
The Meetily command-line tool.
Exports.
Speakers you have not named show as Host (your microphone) and Guest (everyone else). To see how speaker names are added, read about speaker diarization.
Bug Fixes

meetilypro:// links on Mac. Links now work when Meetily is closed. The link opens Meetily and then does what it says. Links that open a meeting or start a recording need meetilypro:// links turned on under Settings > Integrations > Advanced. License activation links always work.
License links during setup. If you click a license link while you set up Meetily, your key is filled in on the license step.
Claude Desktop on Windows. Claude Desktop installed from the Microsoft Store now shows up in Integrations. Before, Meetily could not find it.
Upgrade
If you use Meetily 1.11.0, the app prompts you to update through the in-app update dialog. Click Update Now! to install. All existing settings, recordings and models are kept.

Frequently Asked Questions
Frequently Asked Questions

children.q: Is Meetily Pro 1.11.1 a big update?
children.a: No. It is a fix release with no breaking changes and nothing to migrate. It fixes summaries for long meetings with Built-in AI, makes recordings safer when a save fails, and adds easier access to summary templates.

children.q: Why did my long meeting fail with "Failed to add token to batch"?
children.a: With Built-in AI, the transcript was too long for the model to read in one go. Meetily Pro 1.11.1 splits a long transcript into parts sooner, before it gets too long for the model, then summarizes each part and combines them into one summary. A long meeting now takes longer to summarize, and on a laptop a very long one can take half an hour or more.

children.q: Can I still lose a recording if saving fails?
children.a: Meetily saves your audio in small pieces while you record and joins them when you stop. In 1.11.1, if saving one piece fails, Meetily recovers and keeps saving the rest, so one failed save no longer puts the whole recording at risk.

children.q: Where are summary templates in Meetily Pro?
children.a: Click the Summary Template button next to Model Settings on the meeting page, or open Settings > Summary.

children.q: Do speaker names show in Claude and other AI assistants?
children.a: Yes. When you name the speakers in a meeting, the names show to your AI assistant when it is connected to Meetily, in the command-line tool, and in exports. Speakers you have not named show as Host and Guest.

children.q: How do I update to Meetily Pro 1.11.1?
children.a: Meetily shows an in-app update dialog; click Update Now! to install. Your settings, recordings and models are kept. You can also download the installer for macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows from the Meetily Pro downloads page.
